Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is from this called-off game, where the rain gods won. However, the warm-up game between India Women and England Women is happening at the moment, in Bengaluru. England are 249/3 in 40 overs, with Nat Sciver-Brunt scoring a hundred, and Emma Lamb crossing fifty, and both are unbeaten. You can just switch tabs to enjoy all the coverage of that game. Cheers!

Bad news, folks! The inevitable has happened, and THE MATCH HAS BEEN ABANDONED! We could get only 9 overs of play, which is not ideal for a warm-up for any team, but the weather is not in anyone's control, and we just have to accept the fate. Well, after electing to bat first, South Africa Women did not get to a good start, losing Laura Wolvaardt on the very first ball. Tazmin Brits ​​​​and Marizanne Kapp were among the runs, but they ended up losing three wickets before the rain break. Bangladesh Women will actually be happy, as Marufa Akter made the new ball talk, swinging it both ways and troubling the batters, getting two scalps. Nahida Akter also chipped in with one, but that was all the action that we managed to get in this game.

UPDATE - 6.08 pm IST (12.38 pm GMT) - The visuals are still showing that it is raining, and there is not a single soul around the ground. Also, as we have already lost more than two hours, even if we get a restart, we are bound to lose overs. However, as this is a warm-up match, the players from either side would not want to take a risk of playing on a wet outfield and risk being ruled out of the main tournament due to an injury. So, the match officials need to priortise players' safety first before taking any decision, that is of course if the rain stops.

UPDATE - 5.43 pm IST (12.13 pm GMT) - Nothing positive as of now, as it is still pelting down in Colombo. The other warm-up game, between Pakistan Women and Sri Lanka Women, at the R. Premadasa Stadium, has also been interrupted due to heavy rain. As of now, chances look very bleak for the rain to cede. While we wait for some good news from here, let's take a tour elsewhere. In the Asia Cup 2025, in Dubai, the Super 4 stage is in full swing. India have already marched into the finale, and tonight, it will be Bangladesh taking on Pakistan in a do-or-die clash. That game will begin at 2.30 pm GMT, in just a couple of hours from now. A win for either side seals their spot in the finale against India on Sunday, 28th September. But up in Bengaluru, warm-up game number 4, between India Women and England Women is currently underway with the England Women batting first. There was a bit of a rain interruption in that match as well, but not for long. You can hop tabs and follow all the live action from that match.

UPDATE - 5.12 pm IST (11.42 am GMT) - Scratch the previous update, folks! RAIN IS BACK! And so are the covers as well. In fact, live visuals show that it has gotten very dark out there and the floodlights are on as well. This has been some parade for the ground staff. They peeled off the covers just a few minutes back, but are forced to place them back on the pitch and squares. It is a heavy downpour as of now, and all we can do is pray for the rain to stop. Stay tuned for further updates.

UPDATE - 4.55 pm IST (11.25 am GMT) - Well, good news! It is not raining anymore, and the ground staff have removed the covers as well. However, the umpires are out there inspecting the outfield, which has taken a lot of water, and maybe there are a few wet patches that need a look at before we resume play. We should not be that far away from a restart here.

UPDATE - 4.40 pm IST (11.10 am GMT) - Nothing new from the middle, it is still drizzling. The ground staff are ready to get into action once the rain stops completely. However, the forecast does not look that promising, so we can only hope that once it gets clear, if it does, then we do not face any more stoppages. Stick with us for more news.

UPDATE - 4.12 pm IST (10.42 am GMT) - A bit of positive news! The intensity of the rain has come down massively, and the conditions have brightened up as well. However, the covers are firmly placed on the pitch and the squares. It has been around more than half an hour, which means the ground might have absorbed a lot of water. If and when the rain stops, the ground staff will have to work hard to improve the conditions for play to resume.

UPDATE - 3.49 pm IST (10.19 am GMT) - Uh..oh! It has started to rain here in Colombo, and the umpires have given the marching orders to the players. The ground staff rush out in the middle and quickly put on the covers as it is now pouring down. Stay tuned for further updates.

South Africa Women, meanwhile, arrive with momentum on their side. They recently conquered Pakistan in a 2-1 ODI series win and followed it up by beating West Indies Women with the same scoreline, both away from home. Laura Wolvaardt will take charge of the squad, backed by seasoned stars such as Marizanne Kapp, Tazmin Brits, and Chloe Tryon. With Ayabonga Khaka leading a balanced bowling unit across pace and spin attack, they boast a well-rounded unit ready for action. Stay tuned for the toss and team updates.

Bangladesh Women shone brightly in the ICC Women’s World Cup Qualifier, finishing second to book their spot in the main event. Skipper Nigar Sultana Joty and Sharmin Akhter led the way with the bat, while Fahima Khatun and Rabeya Khan impressed with their spells. The challenge now steps up a notch, as this side prepares to prove itself against stronger opposition on the biggest stage.

Each side will get at least two warm-up games. More than just practice, these contests serve as a reality check to see exactly where they stand. The World Cup itself will follow a round-robin format with eight teams facing each other once, and the top four progressing to the semifinals. That is still some distance away, so for now, let’s turn our attention to the action at hand.
